maria.dev: Hey team — seeing dup POSTs from the onboarding sample app. Looks like two simultaneous token refreshes then both original uploads replayed -> duplicate records. Repro on Android 12 emulator, cold start + quick network toggle. Anyone seen a refresh stampede like this?

alexg: Yikes. Are you using an OkHttp Interceptor or an Authenticator? Interceptor + suspend refresh can race.

maria.dev: Using an Interceptor. Simplified code: ```override fun intercept(chain): Response { if (tokenExpired()) { token = refreshToken() } return chain.proceed(chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $token").build()) }``` refreshToken is a suspend function that calls our auth endpoint. We tried synchronized(lock) around refresh but still saw two refreshes.

sam: Interceptors run on OkHttp dispatcher threads; mixing suspend here is fragile. Authenticator is the recommended path for 401 handling because OkHttp will serialize retries for you. If you must use an interceptor, protect refresh with a Mutex or a single-flight mechanism.

jordan: Also watch WorkManager retries — if the worker is rescheduled while a refresh is in-flight you can get two flows refreshing. We had that exact pattern: worker A started refresh, worker B retries the upload and triggers refresh again. Solution: central token store + Mutex.withLock or expose a shared Deferred for the current refresh.

alexg: +1 for idempotency keys on uploads too — makes duplicates tolerable. Also ensure refreshToken handles exceptions and returns a clear error so WorkManager doesn't blindly retry.

maria.dev: Is there a recommended helper in the android-sdk for "single-flight refresh"? Docs didn't show one and sample app uses Interceptor which might be misleading.

ci-bot: Added a small sample: devex/samples/token-refresh-mutex.kt in PR #3421 by @alexg :thumbsup:

maria.dev: Great — I'll try switching to an Authenticator + Mutex and add an idempotency key to uploads. Will paste logs if it still reproes. Thanks!
